cache-flow.title: Cache-aside pattern
cache-flow.description: The app checks the cache first and only falls back to the database on a miss

nodes.label: Client
nodes.explanation: A user's browser or app making a request for data

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Your application. On each read it checks the cache first; only on a miss does it query the database, then stores the result back in the cache.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.explanation: A fast in-memory store holding recently used data. Answers in microseconds when the data is present (a cache hit).

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: The source of truth on disk. Slower, but always correct. Hit only when the cache misses.

load-balancer-fanout.title: One entry point, many servers
load-balancer-fanout.description: The load balancer spreads requests across identical servers and routes around unhealthy ones

nodes.label: Clients
nodes.explanation: All incoming traffic points at one address — the load balancer — instead of any individual server.

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Distributes each request across the pool of servers (e.g. round-robin or least-connections) and runs health checks so it never sends traffic to a dead server.

nodes.label: Server 1
nodes.explanation: One of several interchangeable servers running the same application code.

nodes.label: Server 2
nodes.explanation: Another identical server. If it fails a health check, the load balancer simply stops routing to it.

nodes.label: Server 3
nodes.explanation: Adding more servers behind the balancer is how the system scales horizontally.

sharding-split.title: Data split across shards
sharding-split.description: A shard key decides which database holds each row

nodes.label: Router
nodes.explanation: Application logic (or a proxy) that reads the shard key on each request and routes it to the shard that owns that data.

nodes.label: Shard A
nodes.explanation: Holds users A–H. A complete, independent database — just a slice of the whole.

nodes.label: Shard B
nodes.explanation: Holds users I–P. Its own server, CPU, and disk — so load is split, not stacked.

nodes.label: Shard C
nodes.explanation: Holds users Q–Z. Add a shard and you add capacity for both data and traffic.
